correctness.rationale: For distinct column roots the Vandermonde factor is nonzero. The alternant quotient is an integer Schur polynomial, equal to h₂ for exponents 0,1,2,5. Every 2p^k-th root has a unique product representation as a sign times a p^k-th root. A vanishing Schur value therefore makes the integer polynomial formed by replacing the p^k-th root with X divisible by Φ_{p^k}; evaluation at 1 gives a signed Schur value divisible by p. This proves the general sufficient criterion, with distinct rows and N greater than the largest row. Here h₂ on four signs is (4+(sum of signs)^2)/2, taking values 2,4,10. This proves full spark for every odd p other than 5, including N=6. When p=5, four fifth-root columns make rows 0 and 5 identical for every k. The comparison mask ending in row 4 has quotient h₁ and vanishes on two antipodal column pairs whenever it fits an even order. A fresh integer cyclotomic-remainder replay found 0, 10 and 0 singular minors out of 15, 210 and 1001 at N=6,10,14 respectively, corroborating but not replacing the proof.
residual_risks: Replay is finite. The criterion is sufficient only; full spark does not assert numerical conditioning.

value.rationale: The mask is the next degree after the near-consecutive h₁ mask that fails at every admissible even order. The h₂ transition gives a concrete family of nonconsecutive Fourier samplers with all maximal minors nonzero, over an infinite composite-order family where simple divisor balance is not a general criterion. The signed test provides a reusable sufficient condition beyond this mask; the failure at five alone would not be the contribution.
residual_risks: No stability or conditioning bound is established.
